Each kidney has over a million tubular structures called nephrons.
Nephron is the functional unit of kidney and has two portions – glomerulus and renal tubule.

elements.text: Glomerulus is a tuft of capillaries formed from afferent arterioles, fine branches of renal artery.

elements.text: The renal tubule starts with a double walled Bowman’s capsule and is further differentiated into a proximal convoluted tubule (PCT), Henle’s loop (HL) and distal convoluted tubule (DCT).

elements.text: The DCTs of many nephrons join to a common collecting duct many of which ultimately open into the renal pelvis through the medullary pyramids.
The Bowman’s capsule encloses the glomerulus to form Malpighian or renal corpuscle.

elements.text: Urine formation involves three main processes, i.e., filtration, reabsorption and secretion.

elements.text: A counter current mechanism operates between the two limbs of the loop of Henle and those of vasa recta (capillary parallel to Henle’s loop).

elements.text: The filtrate gets concentrated as it moves down the descending limb but is diluted by the ascending limb.
Electrolytes and urea are retained in the interstitium by this arrangement.

elements.text: Urine is stored in the urinary bladder till a voluntary signal from CNS carries out its release through urethra, i.e., micturition.
Skin, lungs and liver also assist in excretion.
